slides.title: Purpose
bullets: Blood and its parts (plasma, serum) are the material most often taken for biochemical tests.
In a healthy person the chemical composition of plasma is relatively constant; changes in it may show a pathological process in the body.
The aim is to obtain non-haemolysed serum or plasma separated from the cells, so that later measurements are correct.

slides.title: Preparing the patient and drawing blood
bullets: Blood is taken fasting (at least 12 hours after a meal), usually in the morning between 7 and 10 o’clock; if possible before physical exertion and diagnostic procedures.
The request form gives the patient’s name, age and the time of collection.
To prevent haemolysis blood is taken with a dry syringe and a dry (single-use) needle into a dry tube.
The tourniquet is released no later than 1 minute after the vein is punctured.
To avoid foaming, the blood is run slowly from the syringe into the tube.

slides.title: Separating serum
bullets: 1. Tubes brought to the laboratory are closed with a stopper and put into a thermostat for 10–15 minutes to warm to 37 °C.
2. The tube is centrifuged within 10–15 minutes at 1500 rpm.
3. After centrifugation the serum is transferred with pipettes into other clean tubes.
4. The volume of serum released is about 1/3 of the volume of blood taken.
5. A new request form is filled in.

slides.title: Separating plasma
bullets: 1. To prevent clotting an anticoagulant (EDTA, heparin, sodium citrate, oxalate) is put into the tube beforehand.
2. After the blood is drawn the tube is centrifuged for 7–10 minutes at 1500 rpm.
3. The plasma is separated from the blood cells and used for the test.
4. Which anticoagulant is suitable is stated in the instructions of the method (for example, for ALT, urea and glucose — serum or EDTA/heparin plasma).

slides.title: Sources of error and quality control
bullets: Wet or dirty syringes, needles and tubes, a long-applied tourniquet and forceful transfer cause haemolysis.
Separate plasma or serum from the cells as soon as possible; close containers well to prevent evaporation and store only in plastic containers.
If the analysis cannot be done within 4 hours of drawing the blood, the specimen is frozen.
Do not test turbid, haemolysed or lipaemic serum/plasma, or serum with very high bilirubin.
The material is kept until all analyses are finished — the test can be repeated if needed.

slides.title: Not included
bullets: The manual describes running a metal or glass rod along the tube wall to speed up serum separation; it is not included in the slides because it can increase haemolysis.
Instead of the rod follow the laboratory’s approved rule.

slides.title: Safety
bullets: Treat all specimens as potentially containing pathogenic infections.
Wear rubber gloves; never pipette material by mouth — use a rubber bulb.
Balance the tubes in the centrifuge; tubes with chipped edges are discarded.
Needles and sharp objects go into a puncture-proof container.
